findings.summary: C3 freezes exact transcript-derived context, substitutes alternative upstream messages and evaluates them with fixed-continuation replay plus a leave-one-out baseline. This makes historical-event substitution under held continuation an ordinary counterfactual-credit construction, but with stronger replay/rewind privilege than a strict local online SparkBrain mechanism.
sources: Chen et al., Contextual Counterfactual Credit Assignment for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in LLM Collaboration, arXiv:2603.06859 (2026)

findings.summary: COMA uses a centralized critic and a counterfactual baseline that marginalizes one agent's action while holding other agents' actions fixed. Counterfactual marginal-contribution credit is therefore a foundational ordinary multi-agent baseline; any Spark-specific residual must concern native local/online realization under matched privilege rather than the abstract counterfactual principle.
sources: Foerster et al., Counterfactual Multi-Agent Policy Gradients, AAAI 2018, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v32i1.11794

findings.summary: Mu & Najib model concurrent stochastic multi-player games and define retrospective counterfactual responsibility under a strategy profile, allocating responsibility with Shapley values and proving fairness/consistency properties. Stochastic concurrent responsibility itself therefore has an explicit ordinary formal comparator.
sources: Mu & Najib, Counterfactual Reasoning for Responsibility Attribution in Probabilistic Multi-Agent Systems, IJCAI 2026, DOI 10.24963/ijcai.2026/33; arXiv:2605.13077

novelty_or_reduction_impact: STRONGER_REDUCTION_AND_PRIVILEGE_PRESSURE: counterfactual marginal contribution is established in ordinary MARL; exact-context fixed-continuation replay provides a strong counterfactual credit ceiling; concurrent stochastic responsibility has an explicit formal framework.
